fact_check.claim: Cost of Attendance minus Expected Family Contribution equals demonstrated financial need
fact_check.note: FAQ gives the formula 'Cost of Attendance – Expected Family Contribution = Demonstrated Financial Need'.

fact_check.claim: Expected Family Contribution remains consistent unless your family reports significant changes (link supports only this; cost-moves-need sentence is labeled as our reasoning)
fact_check.note: FAQ says EFC 'remains consistent unless your family reports significant changes'. Previous fix applied: the reasoning sentence is outside the link and labeled.

fact_check.claim: Outside scholarships reduce self-help aid (loans or work-study) dollar for dollar; 'until none remains' removed
fact_check.note: FAQ says outside scholarships 'typically reduce self-help aid (student loans or work-study) dollar-for-dollar'. Previous fix applied. Article omits the word 'typically'; minor, not a mismatch of number or rule.

fact_check.claim: Cornell may occasionally need to reduce federal, state or other grants to comply with rules
fact_check.note: FAQ: 'In rare circumstances, Cornell may be required to reduce federal, state, or other grants and scholarships'.

fact_check.claim: Upload scholarship award notification to the Secure Document Upload portal
fact_check.note: FAQ directs students to the Secure Document Upload portal.

fact_check.claim: Standard Student Contribution earned and saved over the summer; may request a loan to replace it via the Undergraduate Student Appeal Form
fact_check.note: FAQ says students unable to earn and save the standard Student Contribution may request a loan to replace this amount through the Undergraduate Student Appeal Form.

fact_check.claim: Continuing U.S. students must complete the CSS Profile and the FAFSA to renew the Cornell aid offer each year
fact_check.note: Page says returning U.S. students must complete both to renew each year.

fact_check.claim: Divorced or separated parents: both parents must complete separate profiles
fact_check.note: Page says custodial and noncustodial parent each complete a separate CSS Profile. Article says 'biological or adoptive parents'; consistent in substance.

fact_check.claim: 2027-28 CSS Profile: as soon as possible after October 1, 2026 and no later than February 2, 2027; FAFSA as soon as possible after October 1, 2026
fact_check.note: Dates match exactly.

fact_check.claim: Avoid uploading documents that have not been requested
fact_check.note: Page says to upload only requested documents.

fact_check.claim: 2026-27 maximum Pell is $7,395
fact_check.note: Page says max Pell stays at $7,395 for 2026-27. Previous fix applied: the 'differ from last year' claim is gone.

fact_check.claim: Pell ineligible at Student Aid Index of $14,790 or more (twice the max Pell); also ineligible if non-federal grants and scholarships equal or exceed cost of attendance
fact_check.note: Both conditions on the page. '$14,790 is twice $7,395' is arithmetic and correct.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Grant-eligible students not affected; Cornell Grant adjusts automatically if Pell changes
fact_check.note: Both statements on the page.

fact_check.claim: Parent PLUS limits $20,000 per year and $65,000 lifetime per student, starting July 1, 2026; undergraduate loan limits unchanged
fact_check.note: Matches. Page also mentions a possible exception for some current students, which the article omits; minor.

fact_check.claim: SAP evaluated annually after final grades post
fact_check.note: Page: evaluated annually at the end of the academic year after final grades post.

fact_check.claim: SAP standards: 67% completion, 2.0 cumulative GPA, 150% maximum timeframe (180 attempted credits for a 120-credit degree)
fact_check.note: All three match.

fact_check.claim: Attempted credits include withdrawals, failures, incompletes and repeated courses
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Failing SAP means loss of aid eligibility with written notification; paying for classes or sitting out a semester does not restore it; approved appeal gives one semester of probation
fact_check.note: Page confirms written (email) notice, the 'neither paying... nor sitting out' language and one semester of probation. The phrase 'loss of eligibility' is the writer's summary of failing SAP; acceptable.

fact_check.claim: Aid office phone 607-255-5145 and finaid@cornell.edu
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: Virtual appointment hours Monday to Friday, 10:00am to 1:00pm and 2:00pm to 4:00pm
fact_check.note: Page lists weekdays 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. and 2:00 to 4:00 p.m. Previous fix applied. The page content I retrieved did not separately confirm 'schedule a counselor appointment online'; low risk, tied to the same hours.

fact_check.claim: Special circumstances appeal asks for a lower expected family contribution based on changes since applying or unusual family situations; needs documentation; case by case
fact_check.note: All three confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Appeals: typical response 10 to 15 business days; reviewed in order received; approved appeals may not result in additional grant aid; no merit aid; does not negotiate
fact_check.note: All quotes confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Daily Sun (Jan 2024): redesigned FAFSA, which replaced EFC with the Student Aid Index, no longer gives extra eligibility when more than one child is in college
fact_check.note: Article says the new FAFSA 'no longer increases students' eligible financial aid if they have siblings in college'. Attributed to the newspaper and not used as the sole basis of a rule about Cornell's own CSS calculation; the added caveat sentence is applied.

fact_check.claim: Kevin Jensen, executive director of Cornell's aid office, said Cornell meets 100 percent of undergraduates' demonstrated need and Cornell grant aid would increase if federal grant aid fell
fact_check.note: Both statements confirmed in the Sun article. Paraphrased, not copied.

fact_check.claim: Missing paperwork is one cause of lost upperclassman aid that uAspire describes; upperclassmen may have to file several forms with different due dates
fact_check.note: Page describes students forgetting to file forms on time and having to fill out five forms with different deadlines. Previous fix applied: the 'nine reasons' claim is gone. Labeled as a general national source.

fact_check.claim: uAspire describes schools that front-load awards but does not name Cornell as one
fact_check.note: uAspire raises front-loading as a concern; Cornell is mentioned only in passing (no merit aid). Article's claim that it does not name Cornell as such a school is correct. 'Describes schools that front-load' is slightly firm for a concern; minor.

beats_top.query: cornell financial aid decreased why aid offer lower than last year
beats_top.why: The search returned no page that diagnoses a lower Cornell offer; the closest official result is the generic Cornell Financial Aid FAQ. Ours opens with the five causes, adds a line-by-line diagnostic table, SAP and Pell numbers, deadlines, the aid office phone and hours, and the appeal steps, and it keeps Cornell-sourced fact separate from our reasoning.
